segments.text:
V. 31.
Leſt the bodies ſhould r•main on the croſs on the ſabbath— Which they would have accounted a Proſanation of any Sabbath, but of that in particular. For that ſabbath was a great day—Being not only a Sabbath, but the ſecond Day of the Feaſt of unleavened Bread (from whence they reckoned the Weeks to Pentecoſt:) And alſo the Day for preſenting and offering the Sheaf of new Corn: So that it was a treble Solemnity.
